title: Ship a standalone deployment with its required static assets
businessContext: Review a focused Next.js application change before it reaches production. The proposed file below contains the defect or unsupported assumption; external application services, where imported, are integration boundaries.
problemStatement: Review the proposed next.config.ts change. Identify the incorrect framework assumption, propose a minimal corrected implementation, and provide evidence for the selected version scope and its 15/16 differences. Explain the interview variation after solving the base task. This is a framework code review: actual rendering, routing and cache behavior must be checked in a real Next.js build, not a browser function sandbox.
starterCode:
export default {output:'standalone'};
// Deployment copies only .next/standalone and assumes all assets are included automatically.

codeReviewFiles.newCode:
export default {output:'standalone'};

constraints: Preserve the stated user behavior and keep trust boundaries explicit.
Use the selected version’s documented API; do not suppress build/type failures to hide the defect.
Start the packaged artifact from an isolated directory.
Request an HTML route, JS/CSS chunks and public assets.
Verify runtime environment configuration and health checks without bundling secrets into NEXT_PUBLIC values.
candidateTasks: Add actionable line-level review comments explaining impact and correction.
Write the corrected file in the local IDE copy; split annotated companion files where instructed.
Record actual build/request/navigation evidence against the acceptance checks and compare version notes.
hints: Standalone output traces the server dependency subset but static/public asset packaging still needs deliberate handling or an external CDN policy.
Start the packaged artifact from an isolated directory.
alternativeApproaches: Set the intended tracing root and include required files outside the app boundary as documented. Audit the packaged artifact instead of copying the whole repository and assuming that is an efficient or secret-safe deployment.
commonMistakes: Verifying only next dev when the behavior depends on production rendering or bundling.
Treating a visible UI state, matcher or TypeScript type as a substitute for server-side validation and authorization.

nextjsPractice.next15: Use patched Next.js 15 and the router family named by the file path. Await request APIs where the App Router contract requires it; validate behavior in a production build.
nextjsPractice.next16: Applies to Next.js 16.4.5. Cache Components is disabled unless the exercise explicitly enables it. The simulator itself remains on 16.4.3.
